# Drawer

> A dialog for a side panel. Non-modal by default, so the page behind it stays usable, or modal through `showModal()`.

`<slab-drawer>` · Overlays · built on `<dialog>`

Docs: https://slab-elements.dev/components/drawer/

## Import

```js
import 'slab-elements/drawer.js';
```

## Usage

```html
<slab-drawer label="Filters">
  …

  <form method="dialog">
    <button>Done</button>
  </form>
</slab-drawer>
```

## Modal or not

Setting `open`, or calling `show()`, opens it non-modally, and the page behind
it stays usable. Calling `showModal()` opens it as a modal, the way it opens a
`<dialog>`: there's a backdrop, focus stays inside, and the rest of the page is
inert until it closes. Try both above.

```js
const drawer = document.querySelector('slab-drawer');

drawer.show(); // The page behind it stays usable.
drawer.showModal(); // The rest of the page goes inert.
```

With `modal`, setting `open` opens it as a modal too, for a framework that
binds `open`.

```html
<slab-drawer label="Filters" modal open>…</slab-drawer>
```

Style a modal one's backdrop through `::part(dialog)::backdrop`, and match one
or the other with `::part(dialog):modal` and `::part(dialog):not(:modal)`.

## Keyboard

| Key    | What it does                                                                                       |
| ------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Escape | Closes the drawer, unless `closedby` is "none".                                                    |
| Tab    | Moves focus on through the drawer and out to the page. When it's modal, focus stays in the drawer. |

## Elements

### `<slab-drawer>`

Import `slab-elements/drawer.js` to register it.

A dialog with no visual styles for a side panel. It's Dialog, so setting `open` or calling `show()` opens it non-modally and the page behind it stays interactive: there's no focus trap, no `::backdrop`, and nothing is made inert. `showModal()` opens it as a modal, with a backdrop, the way it opens a `<dialog>`.

Everything else is Dialog's: `open`, `returnValue`, `close(returnValue)`, a slotted `<form method="dialog">`, the label, focus moving into it when it opens, and "cancel" and "close" from the host. Focus goes back to where it was when it closes, which the `<dialog>` does itself.

A non-modal `<dialog>` ignores Escape unless it has `closedby`, so `closedby` defaults to "closerequest" here. Escape closes it, and "cancel" can still be canceled to keep it open. Set "none" to turn that off, or "any" to also close it on a click outside it.

Which edge it's anchored to, and how it gets there, is how it looks. Position it through `::part(dialog)`.

#### Attributes

| Name         | Type                                | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `closedby`   | `'any' \| 'closerequest' \| 'none'` |         | Passed to the `<dialog>`. "any" closes it on a click outside it where the browser supports that. Browsers that don't ignore it.                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `hide-label` | `boolean`                           | `false` | Hides the label visually and leaves it as the accessible name, for a design that shows the label some other way.                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `label`      | `string`                            |         | Names it. It's the accessible name, and the visible label where there is one.                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `modal`      | `boolean`                           | `false` | Opens it as a modal when `open` is set, as `showModal()` does, for a modal opened declaratively. Not on a native `<dialog>`, where `open` always opens a non-modal one. `show()` and `showModal()` open it as they say whatever it is, and a change while it's open waits for it to open again. |
| `open`       | `boolean`                           | `false` | Whether it's open. Setting it opens it non-modally, as `open` does on a `<dialog>`, unless `modal` is set.                                                                                                                                                                                      |

#### Properties

| Name          | Type     | Description                                                                                               |
| ------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `returnValue` | `string` | The `<dialog>`'s, so `close(returnValue)` and a `<form method="dialog">` set it the way they do natively. |

#### Methods

| Signature                                  | Description                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `close(returnValue?: string): void`        | Closes it, setting `returnValue` to the value given, as a native dialog's `close()` does.                                                                           |
| `requestClose(returnValue?: string): void` | Asks it to close, as a native dialog's `requestClose()` does: "cancel" first, then a close that sets `returnValue` to the value given, unless "cancel" is canceled. |
| `show(): void`                             | Opens it non-modally, as a native dialog's `show()` does.                                                                                                           |
| `showModal(): void`                        | Opens it as a modal, as a native dialog's `showModal()` does, with a backdrop and the rest of the page inert.                                                       |

#### Events

| Name     | Type          | Description                                                                                                                                           |
| -------- | ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `cancel` | `Event`       | When something asks it to close: Escape, a click outside with `closedby="any"`, or `requestClose()`. Cancel it to keep it open, as a native dialog's. |
| `toggle` | `ToggleEvent` | When it opens or closes, as a `ToggleEvent` with `oldState` and `newState` that doesn't bubble, as a popover's does.                                  |
| `close`  | `Event`       | When it closes, as a native dialog's does.                                                                                                            |

#### Slots

| Name      | Type                | Description                      |
| --------- | ------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| `label`   | `Element \| string` | Its heading, in place of `label` |
| (default) | `Element \| string` |                                  |

#### CSS parts

| Name     | Description                                                 |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `dialog` | The native dialog. A modal one's backdrop is its ::backdrop |
| `label`  | The label                                                   |

#### CSS states

| Name           | Description      |
| -------------- | ---------------- |
| `:state(open)` | While it's open. |
